_comment: safety batch B (evaluation & observability platforms) · arize-phoenix · en body · verified 2026-11-06.

axes.model_access: The platform is not tied to model vendors; the evaluation surface has three layers — LLM-as-judge, custom Python and TypeScript evaluators, and deterministic checks (server-evals doc direct-fetched today). The built-in deterministic evaluators contains, exact_match, regex, levenshtein_distance and json_distance **need no LLM and no API key** (fetched the same day). **The full list of judge-side vendor adapters supported was not verified item by item — recorded as unknown.**
axes.runtime: Running the service on your own machine is the main route: `pip install arize-phoenix` or Docker (repo README and PyPI fetched today; requires-python ≥3.11), with a web UI served locally; the repository also ships helm and kustomize directories for your own clusters. The vendor-hosted line is Arize AX, not Phoenix itself (README fetched today).
axes.local_files: Self-hosted, traces and evaluation data stay in your environment and arrive over OpenTelemetry; the platform does not read your local codebase or workspace files. The self-hosting docs area contains deployment-options and configuration subfolders (directory structure fetched today), **but their bodies were not fetched, so external database and object-storage configuration is recorded as unknown.**
axes.background: Server-side evaluators can be attached to datasets and run automatically with experiments, with no local code (server-evals doc fetched today); batch comparison runs on datasets through experiments. Resume-after-shutdown is not a feature surface for this kind of platform. Scheduling, sampling and retry semantics are not on record item by item — unknown.
axes.tools: OpenTelemetry tracing plus Python/JS SDKs (Releases fetched today include @arizeai/phoenix-cli); the in-repo docs areas cover tracing, prompt-engineering, datasets-and-experiments and evaluation (structure fetched today). **MCP support and the outward API surface were not verified in official statements — recorded as unknown.**
axes.context: What is observed is traces and spans; what is evaluated is datasets against experiments (the datasets-and-experiments area holds concepts, how-to and quickstart files, structure fetched today). **Dataset versioning, splits and experiment-comparison semantics were not read — recorded as unknown.**
axes.permissions: The license boundary matters most: ELv2 forbids providing the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service, and enterprise functionality is gated by a license key (LICENSE fetched today). Self-hosting has no account system. **The official docs site and product page returned 403 to this site's fetch channel today, so commercial terms, data usage and training opt-out were not read — recorded as unknown.**
axes.fit: Fits teams already standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want batch comparisons in a notebook or on their own cluster: traces come in first, become datasets, evaluators run with the experiment, and each score links back to its source call. Not a fit for those who only want a hosted console, or who intend to resell Phoenix wrapped as a service (ELv2 forbids that explicitly), or who need a ready-made red-team or compliance-audit surface. This site does not measure scores and does not rank.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs; conclusions cover the capability and license surfaces only.

**Suggested measurements** (three, each pointing at doc bodies we could not fetch):

- Dataset versioning and experiment comparison: with the same dataset and a different judge model, can historical scores still be lined up
- The division of labour between deterministic evaluators and LLM judges: which quality checks can only be blocked by rules
- Self-hosted dependency cost: operational load and backup semantics once an external PostgreSQL and object storage are attached
unknowns:
- Full list of judge-side model vendor adapters
- Dataset versioning, splits and experiment-comparison semantics (doc bodies not fetched)
- External database, object-storage and cluster configuration in self-hosting (bodies not fetched)
- Scheduling, sampling and retry behaviour of evaluation jobs
- MCP support and the outward API surface
- Commercial terms, data usage and training opt-out (product and docs pages returned 403 today)
- Filing-registry search
